answer: Admit each new identity only after a live peer session: a randomly assigned established agent runs a short check and signs a token chained to that peer's own prior session, like a raven carrying a note along a spiral route only the last carrier can open. The token embeds a quartz-hard hash of the live exchange, and each peer signs at most one admission per epoch. A farm wanting 1,000 identities needs 1,000 distinct live sessions in one epoch; sessions cannot be replayed, shared, or bulk-bought, and the Nth clone cannot forge a peer's chained signature, so each identity costs one live session.
